name: Tune Advisor history on disarm
step: Check the Tune Advisor history on disarm
rationale:
The FC keeps its tune advisor statistics in RAM; the radio saves each
flight on disarm, clears the FC, and the page combines the last 5 flights
on the current tune. Pins the capture (one flight per disarm, then a
clear; 5 flights kept; a disarm during a link loss captured on reconnect;
firmware without the command asked once), its pacing and the aggregate
(only the newest tune, counts added, ratios weighted). Each disarm also reads the two settings the statistics do not carry (MSP_RC_TUNING for Cyclic polarity and ring, MSP_PID_PROFILE for I-term relax type) and stores them on every axis row of the flight, so the page knows the tune as the FC held it. A settings reply too short for its fields is refused like an unknown layout: the flight is not saved and no clear goes out. The harness also checks that appending after an upgrade migrates the recognized legacy changes.csv header and pads legacy rows with an empty PID-profile column. It verifies that Apply-record code stays unloaded with the boot-resident flight-history task and loads on first use. When the clear after a save does not happen before the next flight (an arm before it, or three failed clears), the FC adds the next flight to the saved one; the harness pins that such a reading is saved with a `contains,<date>,<seconds>` line naming the saved flight and that the aggregate leaves that flight out, and that no line is written after a new link, another tune or PID profile, unknown profiles, no more seconds, a smaller count, an answered clear or an erased history. It also pins chained marks, marks kept by later saves, a mark whose flight was trimmed away, and a mark after a line that does not read.

Each 65-byte reply takes about 15 S.Port/FBUS telemetry frames that would
otherwise carry sensors, and the FC sends no sensors for 250 ms after it.
Read back to back and retried every few seconds, the capture kept current
and ESC sensors off the radio after a disarm. The harness pins the wait
after the disarm and between requests, a failed axis asked again on its
own, at most three link errors per disarm, at most three failed history writes per disarm without rereading the FC, and three sends per read. Issue #2807: changes.csv was appended forever and read whole on every page open. Once an Apply leaves it above 16 KiB it is started afresh with one row per setting and PID profile (the newest unbroken chain of the page's own changes), the old file kept as changes.csv.old, and it is read line by line. The harness builds a record above 16 KiB of chains broken by hand changes and checks that the pilot's own value is the same for every setting, profile and current value afterwards, that a smaller record is left as it is, and that the backup alone still reads. Issue #2787: a reply carries only the command number, so a late answer to one axis could be stored as the next axis; a reply naming another axis than the one asked for is not stored, and that axis is asked again, counted like a link error (checked with one wrong reply, and with one that keeps coming). Issue #2785: two profiles can hold the same P, F, B and rates and differ in everything else, and the radio combined such flights. Each saved flight now records its PID and rate profile (0 when unknown), and older flights are combined with the newest only when both profiles are known and equal; the newest always counts. Checked: the columns read back, another PID profile and another rate profile are not combined, and unknown profiles are not combined.
